speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our long-standing position remains that the only path to a just and durable peace is a negotiated two-state solution consistent with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We oppose attempts to create new facts on the ground that undermine the prospects for a two-state solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And it is our consistent position that the Israeli settlements in the West Bank are illegal under international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These positions that we have taken and explicitly stated over the last few years have not been universally welcome and even domestically, have elicited active debate.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the point I am trying to make to you is that people may disagree with certain decisions and positions that we take, but I hope you understand why we take these positions, as Mr Foo Cexiang has emphasised.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Taking a position rather than lying low and seeking cover, in fact, aligns with furthering our national interest.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Articulating these positions is part of exercising agency, because we must try to shape the environment and to carve out conditions which are most conducive for the survival and success of small states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I agree with Mr Giam that in this fraught geopolitical environment, the personal touch is still paramount.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Building relationships at a personal level between leaders, political leaders is still the paramount currency of diplomacy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you include officials and civil servants, the number balloons exponentially.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the purpose of travelling is not just to show up, just to fly the flag, but to deepen the personal rapport and trust between leaders and officials and their foreign counterparts, particularly when the views are divergent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It would not resolve the conflict but building reservoirs of trust and understanding reduces the probability of miscommunications and unnecessary conflicts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Having said all that, let me go one more layer of resolution down.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The second workstream is to buttress an even wider network of middle-power partnerships for greater stability.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think in the last couple of years, the need for middle powers, particularly middle powers who share an affinity for international law, multilateralism, free trade, that imperative for middle powers to get together and for us to engage in middle powers has become all the more obvious.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fourth, obviously, we do need to pay attention to our immediate neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And by immediate neighbours, it is Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei – the core of our core.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And fifth, take an overarching view, we need where to do where we can, to reinforce a rules-based international architecture despite the current headwinds.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, again, it is an example of not surrendering to our fates.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Edward Chia, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Shawn Huang and Ms Jessica Tan asked how we will maintain trust with both the US and China, whilst preserving Singapore's strategic options and even while the two superpowers are competing against each other in the realms of security, supply chains, technology and trade.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have a substantial, deep and multi-faceted relationship with the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you check the figures, you will see that it is multiple times more stock of foreign direct investments (FDIs) from the US than the second, third, fourth and fifth investor, even if you add it up.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We purchase US defence equipment and we cooperate closely on countering terrorism and proliferation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are deepening cooperation in critical and emerging technologies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This year, we celebrate 60 years of diplomatic ties with the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Having said that, China is also a vital partner with whom we enjoy a robust and close relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Over most of the last 10 years, it has been our largest trading partner in goods.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We marked 35 years of diplomatic relations last year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, if you stop to think about it, beyond the numbers, we have a unique relationship with China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: China and Singapore are the only two sovereign states in the world with a majority Chinese population, with deep linguistic, culture and historical links.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This presents both opportunities and it is also a burden for us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Because Singapore is an independent multiracial city-state in the heart of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have our own identity, our own political system and our own values.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, our value proposition, even to China, is to be same-same but different, to quote Mr Lim Swee Say.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Same-same, yes, of course, we enjoy the affinity, the linguistic, the shared cultural heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But different, because Singapore's destiny and our value proposition is to be distinct and not yet another small Chinese city.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Therefore, we have to work with both the US and China where our interest coincides and where our interest diverged, we will courteously stand up and say "no".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And when we say "no", both sides must understand it is not personal, but it is based on a principled assessment of Singapore's national interests and that we are not acting as a proxy for one or the other, against them.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So long as we can maintain this, and I speak now from my experience, in fact, so long as we maintain this principled approach, actually, I feel that we come under less pressure because they know this tiny little city-state is one where the more you push them, the more spine and the more firmly they will hold their ground.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And conducting foreign policy on this basis with superpowers, I am telling you from experience, I think this is only way to do it.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The reality is that all countries, including Singapore, will have to find creative ways to work with both the US and China because they are the major powers and they are relevant to our future.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We achieved a new partnership with South Korea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we are deepening relations with more like-minded partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And I want to reassure Mr Lee Hong Chuang that all these moves, beyond the diplomatic field, are also in, to increase access for our local enterprises to overseas markets.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On ASEAN, I agree with Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Valerie Lee that ASEAN has to remain the cornerstone of our foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is a salient platform from which we engage the wider world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For ASEAN to remain relevant, Mr Liang has reminded us that we must deepen our regional integration in order to become more cohesive, more united and credible.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: An integrated ASEAN builds a stable regional platform for Singapore and gives us a voice, more so than a unilateral voice and also the convening power of ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is why we are also pushing hard on key initiatives that bind our ASEAN economies closer together, as emphasised by Mr Yip Hon Weng and Miss Rachel Ong.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are making progress on the ASEAN Power Grid.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is about creating a sustainable, interconnected infrastructure that supports the entire region's continued growth.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope to finalise the agreement this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I believe it will unlock the immense potential of the digital economy in ASEAN in the years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we must also continue to look outward.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We should give all major powers a stake in the stability and prosperity of our region and to ensure that ASEAN remains the partner of choice.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is the logic behind our open, inclusive ASEAN-centred regional architecture.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The more countries invest in ASEAN's collective progress, the more stable we will be.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This balance of power and interest provides small countries like Singapore with more room for manoeuvre than an alternative scenario where there was only a single power dominating our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a heavy responsibility but also an opportunity, an opportunity at a time of turmoil.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will deepen integration, we will promote external partnerships, we will continue to keep the ASEAN region open for business, open to the world, committed to peace, stability and cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have done so over the years, including the current Deputy Secretary-General for the ASEAN Economic Community, Mr Satvinder Singh.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA will continue to curate and facilitate secondments for MFA and other public officers from other Ministries to the ASEAN secretariat and to other international organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This extends our experience and knowledge base of international diplomacy and tradecraft more widely across our civil service.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Strong relations with Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei are critical.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked how we will step up our engagement of with them.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Victor Lye asked how we will strengthen economic coordination with our neighbours through city-based and regional partnerships, given the increasing cross-border activities of Singaporean companies and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It will catalyse green investment in both countries, and we look forward to commemorating 60 years of diplomatic ties in 2027.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With Malaysia, our leaders meet regularly, both formally and informally, for candid discussions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has allowed us to pursue beneficial regional partnerships, including the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone and the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are deepening economic and people-to-people ties with East Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, we will be establishing new consulates, one in Sabah and one in Sarawak shortly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But at the same time, I will also be candid and tell you that we are trying to manage outstanding bilateral issues that are complex that, by definition, have been around for a long time and will take time to resolve.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the fact of the matter is that Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei will always be close permanent neighbours, and we cannot afford to allow spiky issues to undermine our overall positive cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On international organisations, norms and standards, I agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Lee Hong Chuang on the need to protect the global commons and to support multilateralism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Despite the challenges, the rules-based multilateral system ultimately provides the architecture of norms, standards and institutions that protects the global commons and gives all small states a say.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This means, in spite of the headwinds today, we must continue to do our best to build overlapping flexible circles of plurilateral partnerships with like-minded countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Where we can make common calls, we do so and we proceed.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But achieving consensus among 166 members is very difficult.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our strategy is to push the envelope with like-minded partners where we can, who share our commitment to free trade, and we aim for high-ambition agreements that are inclusive and WTO-consistent, so that others can join when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In other words, make common cause, move forward, invite other people to come onboard, always stay open and inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These are examples where you start small, but you can build and expand these platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Beyond trade, we have also built constituencies of support among fellow small states in the UN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Building consensus in a fractured world is difficult but not impossible.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to contribute where we can.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And our nomination of Ambassador Rena Lee as a candidate for Judge in the International Court of Justice reflects our commitment to advancing the international rule of law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Dr Neo Kok Beng has suggested leveraging technology as a soft power.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have in fact been stepping up technology cooperation in our partnerships with other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We work together with others, including at the G20 and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), to shape the norms and standards and, more importantly, open access to technology that can benefit all countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to strengthen such engagements and ensure that Singapore remains an open and trusted hub for technological innovation and scientific collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I tell my foreign counterparts, send your people to us, we will run an open book exercise with you.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will show you how we do it because anyway, the challenge is not in the idea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And to the extent that we can show people what we have done, including our mistakes, and they can modify it and make it relevant to them, that is how we exercise thought leadership and cooperation in this field.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will face more inflection points, and we will have to take more difficult positions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans will have different views on these foreign policy issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Being interested or, as Ms Eileen Chong has said, literate in global issues and understanding Singapore's national interest will help us engage the world with knowledge, understanding and confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do not necessarily have to agree on all our foreign policy stances, but we must agree that these are matters to be discussed and decided by Singaporeans alone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That means keeping a wary eye on foreign interference and influence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: With increased global contestation, foreign actors will want us to align with their views.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Government statements on regional developments have prompted criticisms from foreign netizens who want us to adopt their interpretations of history, and such attempts will continue.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Geopolitical contestation has become a tussle for the hearts and minds in cyberspace as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must be aware and we must exercise caution because we have a diverse population.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And never, never presume that we are immune to the polarisation and fractures in societies elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The world today, more dangerous, more unpredictable than I have ever seen in my decade plus as Foreign Minister.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The global order that used to underpin our success has ended and we do not expect a stable new equilibrium to take shape in 2026 or, even frankly, even the next couple of years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must expect more issues on which we will have to take a difficult stand.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And external and domestic pressures on us will grow.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I also believe that we should take heart.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The challenges we face today are serious, but they are less severe than what Singapore faced in 1965.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We had no hinterland, no resources, no armed forces.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our social cohesion was yet to be forged, and we lived in a volatile and dangerous neighbourhood that regarded us with suspicion.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Despite all this, our Pioneers pressed ahead and they built this country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a narrative that connects Singapore over the decades.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We may be small and improbable, but we have never been afraid to stand up to fight for what we believe in.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Today, we are in a far, far better position in terms of tools and resources.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The first is our domestic unity, although this is work always constantly in progress.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As long as we understand that we are all in this together, as long as we can inoculate ourselves from foreign influence, as long as we can disagree maturely and, ultimately, still forge a domestic consensus, we will continue to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We cannot be bought or bullied by anyone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The second ingredient is our economic vitality and relevance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew said, "Singapore cannot take its relevance for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Small countries perform no vital or irreplaceable function in the international system".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Hence, we must preserve our relevance to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our friends and partners know that we speak honestly and independently.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They know that we are open and welcoming to all.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is a premium in such a world for stability, consistency and respect for the rule of law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must preserve this capability because it keeps us safe and we are a country that can hope for the best, but also prepare for the worst.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, on this note, I thank all Members for your long-standing support for MFA's work as we continue to navigate the challenges, we continue to safeguard Singapore's national interest, and we seize the opportunities in these troubled times.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I began with Thucydides and the cold logic of power.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For all the turbulence in the world, I believe Singapore's destiny is bright, not because of our size or our luck, but because of who we are.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That Singapore spirit – indomitable grit, courage, honesty, discipline, diligence, rectitude and compassion.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is the Singapore spirit that got us here, and it is what will carry us forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   During the debate on the motion of thanks to the President in September last year, I spoke on the weakening of the multilateral rules-based order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Within a short span of five months, that description is now outdated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, there has been a constant barrage of extraordinary headlines concerning international affairs over the last two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: People may no longer feel very shocked when reading about issues like Venezuela or Greenland.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, the UN and other international organisations are still in existence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, despite the pressures created by tariffs, our economy did better than expected last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A key reason why the rules-based international order was effective was that it was backed by the US.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It had supported international organisations, provided global public goods, and rallied many countries in defence of one set of rules for international conduct.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Violations will be punished, with economic sanctions or military action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The international rules-based order therefore introduced a certain degree of restraint and predictability into world affairs, which otherwise would revert to “big fish eat small fish, small fish eat shrimp”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While the new order has yet to emerge – and it is not clear if it will – we can be sure that contestation between big powers will intensify, as will pressure to “choose a side”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This means greater direct and indirect risks for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While the global environment may have evolved, Singapore’s circumstances and identity have not changed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are a multiracial, multi-religious country in the heart of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This means speaking up when sovereignty is undermined in other parts of the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Prosperity – promoting free and open trade, preserving a rules-based trading system, and securing our access to essential supplies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Social cohesion – upholding the multi-ethnic, multi-religious nature of our country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have worked hard at building a strong network of friends and partners in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But since we have our unique societal makeup, identity and history, being true to our national interests means we cannot possibly share identical positions with all of them all of the time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We sometimes have to say no, after careful consideration, to friends and partners who are important to us, or express views that they might not like to hear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This has happened before, and we must expect it to happen again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When it does, we hope Singaporeans can keep calm and carry on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is not easy to achieve, and made more challenging with foreign infiltration of our information space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With a diverse, digitally connected population, Singapore is an attractive and vulnerable target.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The development of advanced digital tools has supercharged the ability of foreign actors to seed narratives and even mount hostile information campaigns to advance their interests, and such activities have clearly stepped up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If you have not watched Lianhe Zaobao’s seven-minute video explaining how AI can be used to generate sensationalised fake news to manipulate viewers’ emotions, I highly encourage you to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We should be particularly careful when we come across content that highlights or appeals to one particular ethnicity over another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On the whole, we should be vigilant towards online commentaries targeted at Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some of these could be attempts to undermine our confidence or exploit our fault lines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The first line of defence against foreign disinformation campaigns is a vigilant and discerning public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is why it is critically important for MFA to engage domestic audiences and explain our positions as best we can.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The old world order may have ended, but that does not mean we should give up on a rules-based approach to international affairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Doing what we can to strengthen multilateralism and international law is still relevant for Singapore as a small state.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, there is a deep vein of pragmatism in the way we view the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have always understood that size and power matter in foreign relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Most importantly, we must stand on our own two feet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We cannot rely on others to secure our interests and our destiny. : Mr Chairman, small states, like Singapore, do not have to be passive bystanders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have agency and can do much to create strategic space for ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Yip Hong Weng and Mr Henry Kwek asked how we are advancing partnerships with middle powers on the geopolitical, trade and technology fronts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Indeed, one key strategy is to strengthen and expand our partnerships with like-minded countries, including major and middle powers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With this circle of trusted friends, we will forge ahead in critical sectors, like defence cooperation, but also in new and exciting domains, such as energy, technology and sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond strengthening Singapore's economic resilience and security, such ties can also bring tangible benefits to Singaporeans and our companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also established a new strategic partnership with the Republic of Korea and deepened our cooperation with the EU.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond our already strong bilateral cooperation in defence and trade, CSP 2.0 will anchor our cooperation with Australia in frontier areas, like cyber, digital, space and AI, for the next decade while strengthening economic resilience in sectors, such as energy, sustainability and supply chains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: An example is our Go-Green Co-Innovation Programme, an initiative under the Singapore-Australia Green Economy Agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under this programme, both governments jointly fund green innovation projects, allowing our companies to work together to develop, test and commercialise technological solutions that drive decarbonisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also working together in the region on the Financing Asia's Transition Partnership (FAST-P) initiative that will help finance Southeast Asia's green transition projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore and New Zealand have joined hands on many groundbreaking initiatives, particularly on trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore, New Zealand and Chile launched the negotiations for the Green Economy Partnership Agreement in October last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It represents a new rules-based trade agreement that aims to support new opportunities for businesses and enhance trade and investment in green sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With India, the fourth largest economy in the world, we have elevated relations to a CSP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A forward-looking roadmap was jointly adopted during Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's official visit to India in September last year to guide the next phase of our cooperation under the CSP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The CSP roadmap outlines concrete commitments to strengthen our partnership in advanced manufacturing, skills development, digitalisation and connectivity across the air, sea and digital domains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Dr Hamid Razak asked about how cooperation with middle powers could be expanded to support broader people-to-people ties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are doing so under the CSP roadmap through scholarships, study visits and internship programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With France, we upgraded bilateral ties to a CSP, Singapore's first such partnership with a European country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The CSP will strengthen cooperation in existing sectors, like defence, trade, education, research and culture, and expand our collaboration in new areas, including decarbonisation, energy, digitalisation and AI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is the EU's first standalone digital trade agreement with another country and Singapore's largest bilateral Digital Economy Agreement to date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also exploring greater cooperation between the EU and ASEAN, as well as between the EU and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This will provide a platform for both sides to leverage our respective technological strengths and deepen cooperation on sustainability, AI, cybersecurity and next-generation energy solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It will also promote exchanges between our youths and institutes of higher learning in the arts, culture and other areas of mutual interest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through the partnership, we also work closely to facilitate two-way agri-food trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also look to do more with Japan as we commemorate the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Given Japan's strengths, we will deepen collaboration in areas, like the digital economy, green transition and emerging technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These partnerships give Singapore greater resilience and ensure that we remain relevant amongst major and middle powers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I mentioned earlier in my Mandarin speech that the first line of defence against foreign influence campaigns is a vigilant and discerning public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is important for Singaporeans to be interested in global affairs so that they can engage the world wisely and confidently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, Singaporeans need to understand Singapore's core interests and look at global affairs through a Singapore lens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Decisions about Singapore's future must be made by Singaporeans and Singaporeans only, free from external manipulation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Foo Cexiang, Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim and Ms Eileen Chong asked about how we can strengthen trust, unity and resilience at home, and spoke about the need to build domestic support for foreign policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government has stepped up engagement efforts with Singaporeans, including students, youths, businesses and grassroot leaders, through closed-door dialogue sessions and workshops to help Singaporeans better understand our operating context and foreign policy considerations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Ang Wei Neng also asked about how MFA is working across the Government to protect Singapore from foreign interference.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We can only act with confidence if Singaporeans are united behind us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: It is increasingly difficult for us to see major countries continue to adhere to the long-established principles of multilateral cooperation, as well as respect for international law and principles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Great powers are now more prepared to flex their military and economic power to pursue their interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: In fact, some feel even less inclined than before to be held legally or morally accountable for their actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Like a ship in the proverbial storm, we will feel the effects of more frequent and intense geopolitical disruptions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: But despite the rough seas, Singapore has the ability and space to chart our own course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We cannot allow ourselves to drift with the wind or waves, as without guidance it is easy to lose our way and drift into international waters.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: If we try to “balance” major powers or choose sides, it means surrendering our ability to determine our own destiny.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Rather, we must find a compass to guide ourselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We must continue to clearly identify and assert our national interests – be it safeguarding our sovereignty or protecting our social cohesion – and use our capabilities to chart the right path.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: While the world has undergone profound shifts, globalisation continues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: A global division of labour is still essential for production at scale.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: However, flows are becoming more selective and partnerships more strategic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We will need to adjust to these changes by staying open, but connecting in smarter, more diversified and resilient ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Singapore cannot journey alone – we must continue to forge partnerships with like-minded countries and deepen our engagement of fast-growing markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This strategy gives Singapore space to seize emerging opportunities and build a resilient economy that continues to create good jobs and new opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: But our success abroad can only be achieved with strength and unity at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As a diverse, multiracial society, Singaporeans will have different views on international developments from time to time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: While we have provided space for such diversity to be expressed, we have not allowed it to become a means to divide us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Rather, Singaporeans have demonstrated their ability to stay united and close ranks on issues of national interest, so that we can secure what is best for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked about the situation in Gaza while Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about Singapore’s support for humanitarian efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Indeed, this humanitarian crisis moved many members of our community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Singaporeans from different races and religions came together, and with local charity organisations, pooled their resources to provide humanitarian assistance for the people in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: It was heartwarming to witness this whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We have continued to work with regional partners in the Middle East, such as Jordan and Egypt, to support the Palestinians in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: For example, through the Republic of Singapore Air Force’s airlifts and airdrops of humanitarian supplies via Jordan, which I had the opportunity to witness first-hand, and the donation of prosthetics through Jordan’s Restoring Hope Initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With Egypt, a medical team was deployed in Cairo in September 2025 to support specialised care for Palestinians receiving treatment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: A few days ago, Minister Balakrishnan and I hosted Palestinian Authority Minister of Finance and Planning Dr Estephan Salameh who was in Singapore on an official visit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Besides expressing his gratitude to the Singapore Government for their generous contributions towards humanitarian assistance in Gaza, he also expressed appreciation for the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package, and the briefings on Singapore’s education system and smart nation journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We look forward to continue sharing Singapore’s experience with the Palestinian Authority in certain areas which may be of interest and assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This spirit of giving extends to other humanitarian crises around the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: When Southeast Asia and South Asia experienced a series of natural disasters last year, Singaporeans likewise stepped up to contribute assistance and support fundraising efforts by the Singapore Red Cross and other charity organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Singapore and Singaporeans’ contributions reflect our shared values as a “we first” society in how we are united to work together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim spoke about strengthening domestic support for foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Our sense of “we” will be more critical than ever.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: The foreign policy positions we take may displease major powers and external countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: While difficult, we make such decisions to support our national interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Foreign actors may impose their narratives or agenda, exploit our differences and pressure us to see and accept their views.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: But we must remain calm in judgement, clear in principle and direction, and confident in our values.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Most importantly, we must stay united and strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Singapore’s success is intertwined with the region and our immediate neighbours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: As in any close relationship, disagreements in views and policies are bound to occur from time to time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: When they do, we manage them on the basis of mutual respect, goodwill and a long-term view of our shared interests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: At the same time, there is much that we have done and will continue to do together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about the emerging domains that we can pursue practical projects on, including at the state or provincial levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Victor Lye asked if MFA could play a stronger role in fostering a connected regional ecosystem so that our enterprises and young professionals can navigate these ecosystems with confidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Gerald Giam called for greater people-to-people ties with our neighbours, particularly among youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We continue to work closely with Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei to expand bilateral cooperation and deepen regional integration, including at the state, provincial and even city levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Such engagements aim to foster a conducive environment for our companies and young professionals to harness new opportunities, strengthen business linkages and people-to-people ties and foster win-win outcomes in strategic sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We look forward to deepening our engagement with East Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: The opening of our new Consulates in Sarawak and Sabah will expand cooperation and unlock greater connectivity, integration and trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: It will also enable the Ministry to provide better consular services to the Singaporeans living and travelling there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This is an example of how we engage state-to-state and city-to-city.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With Indonesia, we will continue to forge win-win partnerships in new and emerging areas like the green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are exploring projects, such as cross-border electricity trade, carbon capture and storage and the development of a sustainable industrial zone in the Riau Islands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are stepping up engagements with the Indonesian provinces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: I visited Batam last year and had constructive meetings with their leadership and key business figures there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This year, we mark the 50th anniversary of defence relations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: I am sure that many generations of our National Servicemen and women remember training in the Temburong forest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: That Brunei continues to allow our soldiers to train on its grounds is not to be taken for granted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We must continue to take this special relationship to higher levels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We look forward to celebrating the 60th anniversary of the Currency Interchangeability Agreement next year, which remains a hallmark of our relationship and a symbol of our mutual trust and shared commitment to facilitate mutual investments, trade and tourism between Singapore and Brunei.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about the continued relevance and importance of ASEAN and Singapore’s role in strengthening integration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: It is a valuable platform for member states to meet and discuss differences constructively and peacefully; and to work together on mutually beneficial issues, such as trade, connectivity and people-to-people links.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We have cooperated effectively, including during the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We will continue to support the Philippines as ASEAN Chair, and work with them to deepen regional integration and promote external partnerships, in the lead-up to Singapore’s ASEAN Chairmanship next year. : Beyond our neighbourhood, we must expand our global footprint.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This includes strengthening longstanding friendships and building new ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We have diversified successfully into fast-growing markets, particularly during COVID-19, where we broadened our food sources, strengthened our supply chains and built resilient economic connections.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng, Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim, Mr Victor Lye and Ms Joan Pereira asked about the Ministry’s plans to engage emerging regions and encourage our citizens and businesses to explore opportunities there.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We have been pursuing a whole-of-Government approach in engaging emerging regions such as Latin America, the Middle East, Africa, Central Asia, South Asia and the Pacific Islands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This includes establishing new embassies and touchpoints and unlocking economic opportunities for our companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are also working to expand people-to-people and cultural exchanges to build mindshare and familiarity of these countries among Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: For example, we are stepping up cooperation with Latin America, including growing our trade and business linkages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This will be our second resident Mission in Latin America and our first in the Spanish-speaking world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We have negotiated Free Trade Agreements with the Pacific Alliance and Mercosur, two of the region’s most prominent trading blocs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Our companies benefit from the increased linkages and access.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: CrimsonLogic is providing digital solutions in the Bahamas, Mexico, Panama, Suriname, and Trinidad and Tobago, while Olam International operates in Brazil, Mexico and Peru to actively diversify our food sources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: With the UAE, we share a Comprehensive Partnership which spans seven clusters, from political and economic affairs to health, sustainable development, and education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We also engage our Middle East counterparts through regular exchanges and multiple ministerial platforms such as those with Oman, Qatar and the UAE.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We have also bolstered our connectivity with countries in the Middle East, which will foster greater business and people-to-people links.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: In Africa, which is a key driver of future global growth, we are also doing more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: In August, I met 14 African ministers and deputy ministers who were in Singapore for the Fifth Singapore-Africa Ministerial Exchange Visit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This was the largest turnout for the exchange visit to date.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: This will be our first diplomatic mission in East Africa and our third in the African continent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: It will support deeper engagement of the African Union, which is based in Addis Ababa, and support our businesses seeking to access new markets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We engage the Pacific regionally through the Pacific Islands Forum in our capacity as a Dialogue Partner, as well as bilaterally with individual Pacific countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Cultural exchanges have increased our familiarity with each other.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: For example, in 2025, a group of Kazakh artistes performed for the first time in the Chingay Parade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We have also deepened technical assistance cooperation with South Asian countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked if the Ministry will be establishing more resident Missions in the regions I mentioned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We are reviewing the need for more resident Missions, taking into account our limited manpower and resource constraints.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Meanwhile, we will continue to explore opportunities to do more in these fast-growing regions, including through our excellent Non-Resident Ambassadors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Mr Chairman, despite the transition to a more tumultuous world, Singapore has agency to shape the future we want.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: But we must know our interests, stay united and we must build on our strengths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Only then can we seize emerging opportunities, secure our place in an evolving world, and build a resilient economy that continues to create good jobs and new opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: The seas may be rough, but with unity as our compass and our strengths as the keel, Singapore will not drift along with global tides.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: We will chart our own course and sail forward with purpose.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
text: Like in Greek mythology, Atlas who bears the weight of the heavens, a small nation survives not by size, but by strength, in unity and with resilience – so will Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, much has been said about the changing international order.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Against the backdrop of a world that is marked by geopolitical competition and great power rivalry, MFA’s work has become more salient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To safeguard Singapore’s national interests, we need to expand our international partnerships and support a rules-based multilateral approach towards solving global challenges like climate change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I will talk about how Singapore supports the development of other countries and how MFA provides consular assistance to Singaporeans who need help overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: At the 2025 S Rajaratnam Lecture, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong set out how Singapore must meet the challenge of an increasingly uncertain world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Rather than retreat, he urged us to “reach out; not to build barriers, but to build bridges”.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We believe in the transformative role of human capital in driving social progress and economic prosperity of a nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through SCP, we built bridges that support and connect countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To a large extent, the SCP is our way of paying it forward after having received assistance from our foreign friends during our early years of Independence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our investment in development partnerships also forms a key part of our strategy to engage with the global South and create future opportunities for collaboration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh asked about strengthening our capacity-building platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have revamped MFA's Development Partnership Directorate to better integrate Singapore's development assistance across Government agencies, international organisations and foundations to deliver the best possible outcomes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are now better able to mobilise Singapore's full ecosystem – combining policy expertise, industry capabilities and practical know-how – and expand our focus to new domains, such as the digital economy and climate resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The ASEAN region is especially important as 60% of the SCP's participants hail from Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Programmes such as the Initiative for ASEAN Integration, aim to narrow the development gap within ASEAN and enhance regional integration, while we tailor customised bilateral programmes for countries' specific development needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our capacity building initiatives in Southeast Asia extend to both major cities as well as cities in the provinces, such as Batam and East Java in Indonesia, as well as Hai Phong and Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One of our key focus is supporting ASEAN's newest member, Timor-Leste, in its capacity-building.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is in Singapore's interest for Timor Leste to become a successful and contributing member of ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The eSTARS package helps to familiarise Timorese officials with important aspects of ASEAN, including key ASEAN economic agreements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For example, MFA co-organised a two-day training programme last year, conducted in Dili by the Institute of Southeast Asian Studies (ISEAS)-ASEAN Studies Centre, on key ASEAN issues and ASEAN's work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Timor-Leste Prime Minister Xanana Gusmão said during his visit to Singapore last year that Singapore's support has made "a real difference" and reflected a friendship that was "measured in actions, not words".

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For the African region, our most recent development assistance programme, the Singapore-Africa Partnership Leading to Growth and Sustainability (SAPLINGS) Package, was launched by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong during his bilateral visit to Ethiopia in November 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Under SAPLINGS, we welcome African officials to visit Singapore on customised study visits and education programmes to learn about our development journey and also, to exchange learning points.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Dr Hamid Razak asked about expanding Singapore's networks with middle powers and international organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are working with like-minded partners to pool our strengths in delivering and developing assistance programmes to third parties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Such partnerships allow us to amplify our contributions and ensure that our development assistance is relevant, sustainable and impactful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have nearly 30 third-country training programmes today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In Latin America, we are partnering Chile, Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and Argentina to deliver courses to officials in ASEAN, Latin America and the Caribbean, on digitalisation, food safety and disaster risk management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our Regional Training Centres in Oman, Jordan and Qatar train officials from Middle East, Asia and Africa on topics, such as public governance and digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Closer to home, we have also refreshed our partnerships with China, Australia and Korea to conduct courses on topics, such as sustainable development and green economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition, we launched a new training programme with New Zealand in 2025 for the Pacific islands on leadership training for the public service.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have also forged development partnerships with international organisations, just to name a few – the United Nations Children's Fund, UN Development Programme, World Health Organization, WTO, World Bank, International Civil Aviation Organization and International Maritime Organization.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: With the IMF, we worked with the IMF-Singapore Training Institute and IMF Pacific Financial Technical Assistance Centre to provide training for senior finance officials from the Pacific Island countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We also started a collaboration with Google to tap on private sector expertise into our programme for AI Policy Leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Collectively, these efforts allow Singapore to play a part in the capacity-building needs of developing countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is especially salient today when there are fewer global resources available to support development assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our programmes and partnerships profile Singapore as a responsible member of the global community and pave the way forward for further collaboration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, even as we expand our external partnerships, we remain deeply focused on our core mission: caring for Singaporeans overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about how MFA is strengthening consular service to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Today, more Singaporeans live, work, study and travel abroad than ever before.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Some encounter unfortunate situations while overseas and require consular assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The nature of consular cases handled by our officers has increased in complexity, as geopolitical conflict and natural disasters can sometimes strike without warning.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To better equip our teams to handle consular cases, MFA is strengthening our capabilities and systems.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are leveraging on digital tools to serve Singaporeans more efficiently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have enhanced our eRegister system so that Singaporeans travelling overseas can now easily eRegister using their Singpass.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have also enhanced our 24/7 Consular Response Centre to provide effective and timely support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The Centre operates around the clock and keeps a watchful eye on developments worldwide, reaching out to Singaporean travellers during emergencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Beyond digital tools, human connection is at the core of MFA's consular work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: When Singaporeans abroad face distress, it helps to hear a Singaporean voice on the line.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our officers, supported by the 24/7 Consular Response Centre, are that first line of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In January 2025, a tour bus carrying 27 people, including 26 Singaporeans, veered off the road in Lofoten, Norway, due to poor driving conditions caused by inclement weather.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Six Singaporeans were injured, with three of them suffering traumatic injuries that required urgent medical treatment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: With the help of our Honorary-Consulate General in Oslo, our MFA staff, Ms Estelle Ho, maintained close contact with the affected Singaporeans and assisted them in reporting lost passports, obtaining temporary travel documents and making police reports.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Estelle stayed in contact with the Singaporeans in distress until their safe return home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In January 2025, our Beijing Mission assisted a family whose non-verbal teenager with special needs went missing in Beijing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our MFA officer, Mr Lin Jiayi, accompanied the parents during their search, coordinated with the local police, assisted in translation and offered practical assistance and emotional support to the family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The teenager was eventually found by local authorities after being missing for 12 hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: During the Hat Yai floods in December 2025, MFA dispatched a Crisis Response Team to assist Singaporeans affected by the floods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This included providing basic necessities, like food and water, to stranded Singaporeans, liaising with their next-of-kin and facilitating their safe return home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: One of our officers helping Singaporeans evacuate to the airport, Mr Ashlyy Ashmadi, was also left stranded overnight in Central Hat Yai when his hired driver refused to return to the airport due to the floods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: He and a Singaporean, whom he was assisting, both ended up finding temporary shelter until they could both safely evacuate the next day.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: So, when Ashlyy said that he understood what Singaporeans were experiencing, he truly meant it!

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: However, in countries where we do not have resident embassies or HCGs, cooperation with our close partners is key.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about the importance of developing partnerships with other countries to provide consular assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Amongst ASEAN Member States, there are standing guidelines on consular assistance where ASEAN Missions render consular assistance to ASEAN nationals who do not have a resident Mission in the country.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Beyond this, we also partner other friendly countries on the consular front.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For example, MFA facilitated the evacuation of 11 Singaporeans from Iran during the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: While Singapore does not have a resident Mission in Iran, MFA worked closely with the governments of Oman and Malaysia to evacuate four of the eleven Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our officers, based in Missions around the world, including in countries with active conflict, sometimes face real danger.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The team at the Singapore Embassy in Doha were in the vicinity of an airstrike last year and experienced loud explosions and tremors while at work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MFA officers in Moscow and Tel Aviv have had to seek shelter during drone attacks on their host cities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Despite these dangerous moments, our officers have never once asked to leave their posts to come home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Consular work is not easy, but MFA officers, like Estelle, Jia Yi and Ashlyy, do this out of a deep sense of desire and responsibility to help Singaporeans in times of need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I have been with MFA for eight months and I am tremendously proud to be part of the MFA team.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to ask Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, how would she describe Singapore's current relationship with China against the backdrop of Sino-US geopolitical tensions.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Recently we have seen many sharp criticisms targeting Singapore on the internet, especially from Chinese language videos.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: What impact does this have on our bilateral relations?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Apart from Lianhe Zaobao's seven-minute video, how does the Government help Singaporeans guard against those AI-generated videos that seek to divide our people? : Chairman, in English please.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Separately, I would like to ask the Minister whether the current unrest in Mexico will affect the timeline and resolve to open the resident embassy in Mexico?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann first, followed by Minister Vivian.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: (In Mandarin):   I thank Mr Ang Wei Neng for his question.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We share multifaceted cooperation, and our areas of collaboration are wide-ranging.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Regarding the videos Mr Ang mentioned, such content often draws from a wide array of online sources, and we may not always know where this information originates from.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, I believe the most important point is that Singaporeans should remain vigilant when encountering such material.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singaporeans must have a clear understanding of our core national interests.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We must safeguard Singapore’s independence and sovereignty, as well as our security and prosperity.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is actually not difficult to verify the authenticity of online information.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: There is no need to assume that a story is true simply because its headline is eye-catching or its content is sensational.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In fact, the more sensational the headline, the more likely it is that the content may be false.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: A quick search would be enough to determine that these claims are entirely untrue.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, if we rush to share them, we may end up being tricked.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
